title: Fate of Discrete Time Crystals in Finite-Size Cavity QED Systems
abstract: It has been shown that Discrete Time Crystal (DTC) behavior may arise in the periodically driven, open Dicke model in the thermodynamic limit ($N \rightarrow \infty$). In this work, we demonstrate that finite $N$ non-mean-field fluctuations in this model can lead to decay rates and amplitudes of transient DTCs that display a non-trivial non-monotonic behavior with an increasing number of atoms. We show that the second-order cumulant expansion fails to capture the finite-size dynamics, while a stochastic version of the Truncated Wigner Approximation (TWA) is remarkably accurate, particularly in the large atom ensemble limit. Using the TWA and the Monte Carlo Wave Function (MCWF) approach, we identify three distinct dynamical regimes of transient DTC behavior in the finite-size Dicke model. We outline the mechanism behind the non-monotonic finite size dynamical decay of DTC order and discuss the implications for experiments performed on finite-sized atomic assemblies.
summary: This paper analyzes the stability of Discrete Time Crystals in finite-size cavity QED systems modeled by the open Dicke model. The authors demonstrate that simple mean-field theories fail to capture the dynamics, showing that non-mean-field fluctuations lead to a non-monotonic decay of the DTC order parameter as the system size changes. They establish the TWA as a superior simulation tool for this complex, open quantum system.
main_problem: The paper investigates the stability and decay of Discrete Time Crystal (DTC) behavior in finite-size quantum systems, contrasting these findings with predictions made in the thermodynamic limit.
main_result: Finite-size, non-mean-field fluctuations cause the DTC decay rates to exhibit a non-trivial, non-monotonic dependence on the number of atoms ($N$).
method: The study employs advanced quantum simulation techniques, comparing the accuracy of the Truncated Wigner Approximation (TWA) against the Second-Order Cumulant Expansion (CE) and exact methods.
model_or_system: The system is an open Dicke model describing $N$ two-state atoms coupled to a lossy cavity mode, governed by a Lindblad master equation with periodic driving.
key_observables: DTC order parameter ($\langle\sigma_xangle$), decay rates, amplitudes, and the comparison of stroboscopic attractors across different $N$.
important_parameters: System size ($N$), cavity loss rate ($\kappa$), driving frequency ($\lambda_0$), and the comparison between mean-field ($N 	o \infty$) and finite-$N$ regimes.
main_assumptions: The TWA is used as the primary tool for large $N$, while the failure of the cumulant expansions (FSC/PSC) due to Gaussian assumptions is a key limitation noted.
figures_summary: Figures compare $\langle\sigma_x(t)angle$ dynamics across different methods (exact, TWA, FSC) for varying $N$, and show phase space analysis revealing non-monotonic scaling of DTC stability with $N$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the model and comparing simulation methods (TWA vs. CE). It then analyzes the three dynamical regimes (unstable, transient, pre-thermal DTC) and culminates in a detailed analysis of how finite-size effects cause non-monotonic scaling of the DTC order parameter.
why_interesting: This work provides crucial insights into how finite-size effects and quantum fluctuations modify macroscopic quantum phenomena like DTCs, which is vital for designing realistic quantum experiments using finite atomic ensembles.
